newsitem.title: UK: Conoco starts UK Banff oilfield in six-month test.
newsitem.headline: Conoco starts UK Banff oilfield in six-month test.

text.p: U.S. company Conoco said on Monday it had brought onstream first production from the U.K. North Sea Banff oilfield for a six-month test ahead of full development.
Banff, expected to reach a peak of 35,000 barrels per day (bpd) under the first phase of production, came onstream on Saturday, Conoco said.
Banff crude is pumped via the Sedco 707 floating production system and exported on the 750,000-barrel capacity Stena Savonita shuttle tanker.
The early production system will be used for six months, both to recover oil and to gather data to optimise full development of the field, targetted for the first half of 1998.
The field, discovered in 1991, was brought onstream under the extended test just 10 months after receiving government consent.
"The Banff field is important because it heralds a new era of oil production for Conoco in the U.K.," said George Watkins, chairman of Conoco (UK) Ltd.

"It is an example of how new and better technology and business practices, supported by close cooperation between owners, contractors and the government, benefit the economy by enabling the development of smaller discoveries which previously were considered uneconomic."
Conoco is a unit of DuPont Co. --London newsroom +44 171 542 8060
